$comment: Annotated example for run_handoff_sessions.ps1, showing EVERY field.
You almost certainly do not want to start from this file — run `-Init` in your
repo instead, which writes a minimal config with your git root and branch
already detected. Come here to look a field up.
This example is the basic-analysis wave-3 run the script was generalised from,
so every field below has actually been used in anger. Fields marked OPTIONAL
SECRETS NEVER GO IN THIS FILE. It is meant to be committed. Tokens are read
from `envFrom` at preflight and exported to the child sessions.
$comment_repo: OPTIONAL, and best omitted. The runner detects the git root, so leaving this
out keeps the committed config free of any machine-specific path. Set it only
to drive a repository other than the one you are standing in.
$comment_launcher: The session tool, as a SWAPPABLE ADAPTER. Defaults describe Claude Code, so an
unedited config just works; override only the keys you need — the block merges
key by key, so replacing `command` does not lose list/logs/stop.
{{prompt}} is substituted as exactly ONE argument, never split or re-expanded
ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING in `start`: --allowedTools is variadic and swallows
everything up to the next flag, so a prompt placed after it becomes another
'tool name' and the session starts with NO task. Keep {{tools}} before

$comment_worktrees: Both default sensibly: parent directory of `repo`, and repo's own folder name.
$comment_linkDirs: Directories junctioned from the main checkout into every worktree, instead of
being copied or regenerated. Use for generated artifacts that must stay single:
a graphify graph, a model cache. Skipped silently if absent in the main checkout.
$comment_postWorktree: Runs once per newly created worktree, in the configured shell, with {{vars}}
expanded. A fresh worktree is an UNAPPROVED folder: the first session in it
asks to trust the directory and its hooks, and a background session cannot
answer — it goes `blocked` and stays there. Pre-approve it here.
$comment_vars: Free-form passthrough available to briefs, guards and postWorktree as
{{name}}. Values may themselves reference the built-ins: session, key,
sessionName, model, worktree, branch, repo, baseBranch, stateDir.
$comment_subagents: OPT-IN. Rendered into every brief as {{subagentPolicy}}, so all sessions delegate
the same way and the policy is stated exactly once. Omit the block and briefs say
nothing about subagents — a session told to delegate with no cap and no tier
leafRule (default true) stops subagents spawning subagents; without it a wave fans
out geometrically and the budget is gone before the work is.
$comment_sessions: One entry per handoff. `model` is required. `name` defaults to the lowercased
key and decides the branch and worktree names. Each needs `brief` (inline) or
$comment_lanes: Lanes run in PARALLEL; sessions inside a lane run in SEQUENCE. Put sessions
that contend for a resource in the same lane. Omit `lanes` entirely and every
session gets its own lane (maximum parallelism).
Here: E writes the store and A follows it; D and B only read, so they share a lane.
$comment_briefTemplate: Wrapped around each session's brief; {{brief}} is where the session body lands.
This is the DRY seam: the rules every session shares are written ONCE here, and
each session file carries only its own task. Use briefTemplateFile to keep it
in a markdown file instead of this JSON.
$comment_guards: OPT-IN. Omit the whole block and the runner merges on a clean stop alone.
Fully generic: any command. `{{guards}}` in args expands in place to `paths`.
$comment_allowedTools: Headless sessions cannot answer permission prompts, so tools are pre-allowed.
The repo's hooks still run on every call — the hook, not the prompt, is the guard.
NOTE: playwright's tool prefix depends on how it is wired. User-scope server =
$comment_preflight: requirePaths are checked before anything starts. envFrom is a JSON file whose
`env` block is exported to the child sessions — secrets stay in the main
checkout and are never copied into a worktree.
